On arrival, vital signs were temperature of 100.1 F, heart rate - 104/minute, respiratory rate - 26/minute, blood pressure - 79/50 mm Hg, and oxygen saturation of 99% in ambient room air. panels.rationale: Single H&E skin-biopsy section from a human patient. The article title and in-text explicitly diagnose Gianotti-Crosti syndrome ('The child was diagnosed with atypical GCS following hepatitis B vaccination'), and the caption/in-text describe the expected GCS histology: mild acanthosis with a moderately intense superficial/mid-dermal perivascular and periadnexal lympho-histiocytic infiltrate and focal lymphoid exocytosis, matching the spongiotic-dermatitis histology finding. No subtype is defined by the provided vocabulary, so subtype is null. The case is explicitly labeled atypical (vaccine-triggered, recurrent), hence typicality atypical; the histologic pattern itself is the expected GCS pattern. Histology shows no assessable skin tone and no stated ethnicity.
